page.title: Overview
page.blurb: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster through natural language commands.
paras: Claude Code can run one-shot commands, hold an interactive session, or run unattended in CI. It reads the files it needs, runs the commands you allow, and shows you a diff before anything changes on disk.
Install it once and use it in any project folder. There is no per-repository setup beyond an optional CLAUDE.md.
subParas: Install with npm, or with the native installer for macOS, Linux and Windows.

items.title: Claude Code best practices
items.what: Verify-your-work loops, plan mode, CLAUDE.md, subagents and parallel sessions.
items.start: Copy the CLAUDE.md pattern into your own project first. It changes every session after it.

page.title: Claude Code: Best practices for agentic coding
paras: Claude Code is intentionally low-level and unopinionated. That flexibility makes it a blank slate, which can be hard to pick up.
This post covers the patterns that have proven effective across Anthropic's internal teams and the wider community: tuning your setup, giving Claude more tools, and common workflows.
The single highest-leverage change is a CLAUDE.md checked into the repository root. Claude pulls it into context automatically at the start of every session.

page.title: Agent SDK overview
page.blurb: Build custom AI agents on the same agent harness that powers Claude Code.
paras: An agent is an application that completes a task by planning its own steps and calling tools that read files, run commands, or edit code. The SDK gives you the same loop, agent management, and context management that power Claude Code.
It is available in TypeScript and Python, and it exposes the same permission and hook system the CLI uses.
page.callout: If you only need to script Claude rather than build a product around it, the CLI's --print mode is usually enough and takes minutes instead of days.

page.title: What is the Model Context Protocol?
page.blurb: MCP is an open standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.
paras: Using MCP, AI applications like Claude or ChatGPT can connect to data sources, tools and workflows — letting them access key information and get things done.
Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications. It provides a standardised way to connect AI applications to external systems.
page.callout: Servers expose three things: resources to read, tools to call, and prompts to reuse. Most useful servers start with one tool.

items.title: Building effective agents
items.what: The seven agent patterns, named and drawn, with when each one is worth it.
items.start: Read the seven patterns and name the one your current workflow already is.

page.title: Building effective agents
paras: Over the past year, we have worked with dozens of teams building LLM agents across industries. Consistently, the most successful implementations were not using complex frameworks or specialised libraries. They were building with simple, composable patterns.
In this post, we share what we have learned from working with our customers and building agents ourselves, and give practical advice for developers.
The most important distinction is between workflows, where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths, and agents, where the model directs its own process.
